message: Planned a browser action-conditioning demo after capacity selection and context ablation.
Demo launch blocked after the existing DSW A10 stopped and could not restart.
Defined readiness as both a passing health call and one real model-inference step.
Started the medium/context-16 live demo after model and context selection.
Initial demo startup failed because ThreadPrefetchIterDataset was iterable but not an iterator.
Applied commit 58758e5 and restarted only the demo process; training and evaluation artifacts were unchanged.
Remote health passed and the pipeline wrote LIVE_DEMO_READY.json.
The SSH-forwarded health and one real action-7 model step passed; measured step latency was 7412.4 ms.
A second generated step failed with a float32/bfloat16 dynamic_update_slice mismatch, proving that the original one-step readiness check did not exercise autoregressively updated context.
Added a regression contract requiring reset plus two consecutive generated steps; the check failed against the original server.
Restarted only the demo with generated latents cast back to the existing bfloat16 context dtype before concatenation; checkpoint and sampling protocol were unchanged.
Health plus reset and two consecutive model steps passed through the SSH tunnel. This supersedes the earlier implication that a single successful step established sustained interaction.
Committed the dtype recovery, two-step regression checks and retained failure/recovery evidence to the experiment-ledger branch.
After local, live-runtime and GitHub CI validation, replaced the one-hour recovery timer with the final three-hour user evaluation window.
